newsitem.title: UK: Dlr edges up in Europe after tame German M3 growth.
newsitem.headline: Dlr edges up in Europe after tame German M3 growth.

text.p: The dollar gained against the mark in morning Europe after news lower-than-expected German M3 money supply growth further dampened speculation German rates will rise soon, traders said.
The Bundesbank said July M3 grew an annualised 5.7 percent versus fourth-quarter 1996, down from 6.4 percent in June. Economists polled by Reuters had expected money supply to grow 6.3 percent.
The dollar had eased to session lows earlier when short-term investors took profits after the Bundesbank kept its repo rate steady at 3.00 percent.

"The M3 figures take any pressure away from the Bundesbank to raise German rates soon and as a consequence the mark should soften," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International. Rate rise speculation had already been dampened late on Monday after Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said an increase now would be very damaging for the economy. Recent mark weakness was worrying but that there were no sufficient signs that inflation was speeding up to warrant a rise, he said.
The dollar was at 1.8368/78 at 0855 GMT, up from 1.8355/65 at Monday's European close and from a low of 1.8315 hit shortly after the repo annoucement.
"The market will still look to Thursday's Bundesbank council meeting but if there ever was a chance of a rate change it's even slimmer now," said Stamenkovic.
U.S. rates are also expected to remain on hold at Tuesay's meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee as inflationary pressures on the U.S. economy remain benign, analysts said.

Dollar/yen was at 118.01/08 from 117.95/05 in late Europe. Dealers said the sharply weaker mark/yen cross was weighing on dollar/yen. Mark/yen dropped from around 64.40 at the open to 64.15/18 at 0807 GMT, compared with 64.44 in late trade on Monday. It failed to break key resistance at 64.90/65 on Monday.
With German rate rise speculation now dampened the market is looking for direction, traders said.

The recent strengthening of the mark - it is now almost six pfennigs below its recent peak just above 1.89 marks and has strengthened on its European crosses - has eased the need to tighten German rates to strengthen the mark.
Signs of improvements in Germany's economy, however, are likely to refuel rate rise speculation, analysts said.

The Ifo-Institute business sentiment index - scheduled for release on Wednesday - is expected to rise from 96.0 in June. A Reuters poll of economists showed a range of forecasts between 96.4 and 97.2.
News overnight that United Parcel Service (UPS) had reached a tentative pact with the Teamsters union to end its 15-day strike had limited impact on currencies overnight.
But dealers said they would watch U.S. Treasuries as the news might raise concerns about wage inflation in the U.S. and could depress bond prices.
